title: Tipalti Pricing in 2026: What It Actually Costs
summary: Tipalti pricing starts at $99/month for AP, but the real cost is transaction and FX fees. The pricing model, entity fees, implementation, and total cost, broken down.
body_markdown:
Tipalti is one of the most capable global accounts payable and mass-payment platforms, and it is more transparent than most about its entry price, but far less so about what you will actually pay. It publishes a starting platform fee, then everything real is quote-based. That makes **Tipalti pricing** tricky to plan around, because the headline number is just the floor. This guide breaks down the full cost structure so you can size a deal before you talk to a rep.


A note on sourcing: Tipalti's starting platform fees are published, but transaction fees, FX markups, and entity pricing are quote-based. The figures below mark clearly what is vendor-published versus a third-party estimate.


## **How much does Tipalti cost?**


> Tipalti pricing starts at a published platform fee of $99 per month for Accounts Payable and $249 per month for Mass Payments, but that is only the floor. The real cost comes from per-transaction and per-payment fees, an FX markup on cross-border payouts, and fees for additional entities, all of which are quote-based and scale with your payment volume.

## **How Tipalti pricing works**


Tipalti's cost is built from several components that stack up:


- **Platform fee.** A base subscription,[published starting at $99/month for AP and $249/month for Mass Payments](https://tipalti.com/pricing/) , rising with scope.
- **Per-transaction fees.** Fees on each payment, varying by rail (ACH, wire, international).
- **FX markup.** A spread on cross-border payouts, commonly estimated in the 1.9 to 3% range by third parties. This is often the largest hidden cost.
- **Additional entities.** Extra legal entities are billed on top, estimated around $500 to $600 per month each by third parties.
- **Implementation.** A one-time setup fee.


Because the real cost is transaction- and volume-driven, two companies on the same platform fee can pay very different totals depending on how much and where they pay.


## **Tipalti cost estimates**


Component Cost Source


AP platform fee From $99 / month Tipalti (published)


Mass Payments platform fee From $249 / month Tipalti (published)


FX markup (cross-border) ~1.9% to 3% (estimated) Third-party estimate


Additional entity ~$500 to $600 / month (estimated) Third-party estimate


Per-payment fees Varies by rail Quote-based


The published $99 and $249 figures are real but represent the entry floor. For a company paying suppliers at volume, especially internationally, the transaction and FX costs dwarf the platform fee. Get the FX markup and per-payment fees in writing before signing.


## **Is Tipalti worth the price?**


For a company paying many suppliers across borders, Tipalti often is worth it. The automation of global AP, tax and compliance, and mass cross-border payments is genuinely hard to replicate, and at high volume the convenience and control justify the cost.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **How much does Tipalti cost?**


Tipalti publishes starting platform fees of $99 per month for Accounts Payable and $249 per month for Mass Payments. The real cost comes from per-transaction fees, an FX markup on cross-border payouts, and fees for additional entities, all quote-based and scaling with payment volume.


### **What is Tipalti's FX markup?**


Tipalti does not publish its FX markup, but third-party sources commonly estimate it in the 1.9 to 3% range on cross-border payouts. Because it applies to every international payment, it is often the largest cost for companies paying suppliers abroad. Confirm it in writing.


### **Is Tipalti pricing public?**


Partially. The entry platform fees ($99 AP, $249 Mass Payments) are published, but transaction fees, FX markup, entity fees, and implementation are quote-based and depend on your volume and scope.

## **The bottom line**


Tipalti pricing starts at a published $99 to $249 per month, but the real cost is in per-transaction fees, the FX markup on cross-border payouts, and per-entity fees, all of which scale with volume and are quote-based. For a global payer at scale, that buys real value; for a smaller team, the fees can outweigh the benefit.
